title: Mara and the Ledger
premise: In 1847, Dominic Quintana—raised in a pearl-fishing family, indentured since childhood to the Verrone Trading Company's ledger house—has survived by being unremarkable and unheard. When she is ordered to copy a sealed letter, she discovers her own family's village named as the scapegoat in a scheme to cover the company's theft of pearl revenues, with blame timed to fall just before the company's flagship sails. Dominic must decide which silences to break, gathering testimony from divers, clerks, and a disgraced archivist while the company hunts the missing original letter. In the end she smuggles the true ledger and sworn statements aboard the flagship itself, forcing the truth on the record before the morning tide carries the victors' version of history out to sea.
about_author: Mara Montrose is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers in coastal archives, where she first encountered the marginalia of indentured clerks. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, copies routine correspondence in the Verrone ledger house, demonstrating her practiced invisibility and the small kindnesses of the cook, Beatriz, her only friend. Emotional beat: the ache of belonging to no one while belonging everywhere and nowhere.

chapters.title: What the Seal Conceals
chapters.summary: Ordered to prepare a sealed letter for the director's signature, Dominic glimpses her family's village name—Puerto Ceniza—inside. She reseals it, hands shaking. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: the first crack in twelve years of safe silence.

chapters.title: Lessons in Being Unseen
chapters.summary: Flashback to Dominic's indenture at age nine: her father's drowning, her mother's bargain, and the clerk who taught her that ledgers remember what people are forbidden to say. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: grief reframed as survival strategy.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Fell
chapters.summary: Dominic seeks out Tomás Iriarte, a dismissed company archivist now mending nets, who once accused Verrone of falsified pearl weights. He warns her that documents without protectors are just paper. POV Tomás. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two people erased by the same institution.

chapters.title: Weights and Measures
chapters.summary: Dominic audits the pearl ledgers and finds the pattern: systematic underweighting of divers' catches, the shortfall laundered into a fictitious 'Ceniza debt.' POV Dominic. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the theft is arithmetic, and arithmetic can be proven.

chapters.title: A Letter Home That Never Goes
chapters.summary: Dominic writes to her mother, then burns the letter, knowing the company reads outbound post. She decides to travel to Ceniza under pretext of a records audit. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Road to Ceniza
chapters.summary: Traveling with company escort Rivas, who may be a minder or a potential ally, Dominic sees the poverty her ledgers helped conceal. POV Rivas. Emotional beat: his dawning complicity and quiet shame.

chapters.title: Salt and Memory
chapters.summary: In Ceniza, Dominic's mother recognizes her but cannot embrace her before the escort; the divers speak in the old silences. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: home as a language she can still read but no longer speak.

chapters.title: The Divers' Count
chapters.summary: The divers produce their own tally-sticks, kept for twelve years in a church wall, recording every underweighted catch. POV her mother, Serafina. Emotional beat: the poor keep their own ledgers of the heart.

chapters.title: Rivas Chooses
chapters.summary: Rivas discovers Dominic copying the tally-sticks and, instead of reporting her, falsifies the escort log to buy her time. POV Rivas. Emotional beat: a small betrayal of the company becomes a large act of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Director's Shadow
chapters.summary: In the capital, director Aurelio Verrone learns of the Ceniza audit and orders the flagship's departure moved up—and a fire 'inspection' for the ledger house. POV Aurelio. Emotional beat: villainy as tidy bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Ash in the Margins
chapters.summary: Beatriz warns Dominic by coded laundry-line signal; the ledger house burns, destroying the originals. Dominic realizes the sealed letter's copy in her memory and the tally-sticks are now the only record. POV Beatriz. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Fugitive Clerk
chapters.summary: Dominic, Tomás, and Beatriz hide in the fish market's ice cellar, reconstructing figures from memory onto any paper they can find. POV Tomás. Emotional beat: found family forged in hiding.

chapters.title: The Notary's Price
chapters.summary: They need sworn certification; the only notary willing is a woman, Inés Solano, whose brother died diving for Verrone. She demands the whole truth in her record, no softening. POV Inés. Emotional beat: grief converted into professional fury.

chapters.title: What Serafina Swears
chapters.summary: Serafina arrives in the city to give testimony, and mother and daughter finally speak plainly—about the indenture, the silence, the years. POV Serafina. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Rivas is caught and interrogated; under pressure he reveals the ice cellar. The group scatters, and Tomás is taken, the reconstructed ledger seized. POV Rivas. Emotional beat: guilt, and the fear that sacrifice was wasted.

chapters.title: The Second Original
chapters.summary: Tomás, in custody, reveals he memorized the figures years ago—his accusation failed for lack of a witness, not a record. Dominic realizes testimony plus tally-sticks plus a notary can still stand. POV Tomás. Emotional beat: hope rebuilt on failure's bones.

chapters.title: Boarding the Flagship
chapters.summary: Disguised as a supernumerary clerk, Dominic carries the certified deposition aboard the Verrone flagship the night before sailing, aided by Beatriz's kitchen access. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: terror and purpose in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Captain's Cabin
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts Aurelio aboard; he offers her freedom, wages, a name. She answers with the deposition and Inés's seal, and places a copy with the harbormaster's office as insurance. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: the silence finally broken, at full voice.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Aurelio orders the ship to sail anyway, betting the port will bend—but Rivas, released, delivers the harbormaster's copy to the colonial magistrate, and the flagship is held at anchor under investigation. POV Rivas. Emotional beat: the machine of history jammed by ordinary courage.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: The inquiry opens; divers testify with Inés translating, Tomás's memory corroborated by the tally-sticks. Verrone's falsified ledgers unravel. Aurelio is remanded; the divers' contracts voided. POV Inés. Emotional beat: justice as slow, imperfect, but real.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Our Own
chapters.summary: A year later, Dominic—indenture dissolved—opens a free notary and record house with Inés and Beatriz; Serafina tends the first entry: the divers' true names and true weights. POV Dominic. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, written in her own hand.
